ai.description: This caecilian reaches 30 cm. It is dark grey to purple-brown with a pale snout and vent. It is distinguished by its primary annuli and lack of secondary grooves.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Gegeneophis ramaswamii* is best distinguished by its lack of secondary grooves and its uniquely high count of primary annuli (120–130), setting it apart from other Indian caecilians.
ai.habitat: *Gegeneophis ramaswamii* inhabits moist, loose soil in tropical evergreen forests and agricultural plantations across the Western Ghats at altitudes of 200–1,000 meters.
ai.behavior: The Tenmalai caecilian is primarily nocturnal, emerging from its subterranean burrows at night to forage for earthworms and other small soil-dwelling invertebrates.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Gegeneophis ramaswamii* is oviparous, laying 15–25 eggs in underground nests during the monsoon season (June–August), which the female guards until they hatch.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Gegeneophis ramaswamii* is endemic to the southern Western Ghats in Kerala, India, typically found at elevations between 200 and 1,000 meters.
ai.callDescription: The Tenmalai Caecilian produces a series of low-frequency, rhythmic clicks or pulses, typically emitted from within moist soil or leaf litter in its humid forest habitat.
